question.text: How many Swiss regions will be classified as "Extremely Dry" according to the Swiss drought platform on December 1, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the number of Swiss drought regions classified as "Extremely dry" according to the Swiss [National drought platform](https://www.trockenheit.admin.ch/en) when accessed by Metaculus on or after December 1, 2026.

research:
**Bottom line:** As of 1 November 2026, a news report says **3 regions** are "Extremely dry" on the platform: the Lake Zurich region, the Glarus Alps and the Rhine valley. I could not check this against the platform's own list, because the map and list views don't come through in fetched text. Nothing settles the question yet. Rain in October eased the drought, but early November is expected to stay dry.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-02: The platform shows "Situation bis 01.11.2026, Aktualisiert am 02.11.2026". The bulletin headline is "Die Trockenheitssituation hält an" (the drought continues). It says recent rain eased the drought in some regions for now, but the overall situation stays tense. The legend has five classes: not dry, slightly dry, dry, very dry, extremely dry. The regional assignments are only in the interactive map and list view, so I could not count them myself. [trockenheit.admin.ch/de](https://www.trockenheit.admin.ch/de), [EN](https://www.trockenheit.admin.ch/en)
- 2026-11-02: Bote der Urschweiz, citing the federal drought platform: **3 regions** are in extreme drought (Lake Zurich region, Glarus Alps, Rhine valley). Ticino is the only canton where the drought has ended. This is the best available latest value. [bote.ch](https://www.bote.ch/nachrichten/schweizundwelt/wetter-schweiz-winter-wird-wohl-nass-und-mild-art-1729932)
- A search summary suggested most of the Plateau (Mittelland) and the Alps are "dry or very dry". I could not confirm that wording on the page.
- 2026-10-18: The platform's modelled soil-moisture layer (WaSim model) was last updated on this date and showed "extrem trocken" somewhere. I don't know how many regions that covered. [platform soil page](https://www.trockenheit.admin.ch/de/faktoren/boden/modellierte-bodenfeuchte)
- I could not find out how many drought regions the platform has in total. The question's range (up to 25.5) suggests it is at least about 25.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the outcome. The count fell from widespread extreme drought in the summer to about 3 regions by 1 November. Updates appear roughly weekly (updated 02.11 for the situation to 01.11), so several more updates will come before 1 December.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-04: MeteoSwiss says it is a dry day across Switzerland, with fog over the Plateau and sun in Valais. [tdg.ch](https://www.tdg.ch/meteo-soleil-en-valais-grisaille-sur-le-plateau-ce-mercredi-197978571446)
- 2026-11-02: Graubünden moved about 5,000 fish; most river basins hit historic low water levels this summer. [swissinfo](https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/emissions-reduction/gr-around-5000-fish-have-been-relocated-due-to-the-drought/92314947)
- 2026-11-02: Rain has done little for the Rhine, Lake Zurich and Lake Constance, and lake and river levels are still exceptionally low. [bote.ch](https://www.bote.ch/nachrichten/schweizundwelt/wetter-schweiz-winter-wird-wohl-nass-und-mild-art-1729932)
- 2026-11-02: The mushroom season was poor after the hot, dry summer. [bluewin](https://www.bluewin.ch/en/news/switzerland/a-bad-season-for-mushroom-pickers-li.3658361)
- About 2026-10/11: Tages-Anzeiger describes the summer half-year as the driest in about 160 years, with the second-warmest September since 1864 (taken from a search summary; I could not fetch the page). [Tages-Anzeiger](https://www.tagesanzeiger.ch/wetter-schweiz-kommt-im-november-endlich-regen-966057637491)
- 2026-08-26: WSL says that, according to the platform, most of Switzerland was affected by extreme drought. [WSL FAQ](https://www.wsl.ch/de/metanavigation/im-fokus/trockenheit-2026-haeufige-fragen-und-antworten/)
- 2026-08-01: The second-highest drought danger level applied in all Swiss regions. [20 Minuten](https://www.20min.ch/story/historische-hitzewellen-schweiz-trockenheit-duerrejahre-103610162)
- 2026-04-21: MeteoNews said large parts of the Plateau, northwestern Switzerland and parts of Valais were already extremely dry in spring. [MeteoNews](https://meteonews.ch/de/News/N16444/Trockenheit-immer-noch-recht-ausgepr%C3%A4gt)

## 4. Base rates
- 2026 path: extreme drought from spring, covering most of the country in summer (August), then rain in October cut the count to about 3 by 1 November.
- I found no data on past December values. Swiss droughts usually ease in late autumn and winter, when evaporation is low, but low lakes and rivers can keep hydrological drought going (for example, the low Rhine and lakes now).
- I could not find monthly change statistics for the platform's region counts. The October drop shows that big swings within a month are possible.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this. None of the markets you supplied match: they cover the SNB, referendums, the Federal Council and the NY Jets.
- 2026-11-02: Meteorologist Klaus Marquardt (MeteoNews) expects almost no precipitation in the first 10 days of November, just fog and at most drizzle. He says the current El Niño could possibly bring a mild, wet winter. [bote.ch](https://www.bote.ch/nachrichten/schweizundwelt/wetter-schweiz-winter-wird-wohl-nass-und-mild-art-1729932)
- About 2026-10-30: A search summary said wetter.ch cites NOAA's model as forecasting a drier-than-normal November, especially in the south and east. I could not verify this. [wetter.ch](https://www.wetter.ch/)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- About 4 weekly platform updates (around 9, 16, 23 and 30 November).
- Weather in mid to late November: a dry first ten days could make things worse again or stop recovery, while frontal rain or snow later in the month could cut the count. Snow adds less to soil and river flows right away.
- Possible further low-water reports on the Rhine and the lakes. These hydrological factors feed into the platform's classification.

Sources: [trockenheit.admin.ch/de](https://www.trockenheit.admin.ch/de), [trockenheit.admin.ch/en](https://www.trockenheit.admin.ch/en), [bote.ch](https://www.bote.ch/nachrichten/schweizundwelt/wetter-schweiz-winter-wird-wohl-nass-und-mild-art-1729932), [WSL](https://www.wsl.ch/de/metanavigation/im-fokus/trockenheit-2026-haeufige-fragen-und-antworten/), [20min](https://www.20min.ch/story/historische-hitzewellen-schweiz-trockenheit-duerrejahre-103610162), [MeteoNews](https://meteonews.ch/de/News/N16444/Trockenheit-immer-noch-recht-ausgepr%C3%A4gt), [Tages-Anzeiger](https://www.tagesanzeiger.ch/wetter-schweiz-kommt-im-november-endlich-regen-966057637491), [wetter.ch](https://www.wetter.ch/), [swissinfo](https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/emissions-reduction/gr-around-5000-fish-have-been-relocated-due-to-the-drought/92314947), [bluewin](https://www.bluewin.ch/en/news/switzerland/a-bad-season-for-mushroom-pickers-li.3658361), [tdg.ch](https://www.tdg.ch/meteo-soleil-en-valais-grisaille-sur-le-plateau-ce-mercredi-197978571446), [platform soil page](https://www.trockenheit.admin.ch/de/faktoren/boden/modellierte-bodenfeuchte)

I couldn't get an exact count of "extremely dry" regions from the resolution page, because the map can't be read as text. Here is what I found.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-02: The National Drought Platform was updated on 02.11.2026, showing the situation as of 01.11.2026. The headline reads "Die Trockenheitssituation hält an" (the drought continues): recent rain eased things locally, but the overall situation remains tense. It uses five classes: not dry, slightly dry, dry, very dry, extremely dry. Region-by-region classes appear only in the interactive map and the "Display list" view, which my tools could not read. **So I could not get the exact current number of "extremely dry" regions.** [source](https://www.trockenheit.admin.ch/en)
- 2026-08-01: The platform has **38 regions**. On that date there were 20 extremely dry, 13 very dry, 2 dry and 3 slightly dry, citing BAFU (the Federal Office for the Environment). [Blick](https://www.blick.ch/sonntagsblick/wegen-anhaltender-trockenheit-geht-uns-das-trinkwasser-aus-id22151220.html)

## 2. Current status
- 2026-11-02: Citing the federal platform, Bote/CH Media reports that the Lake Zurich area, the Glarus Alps and the Rhine Valley are in extreme drought. Large parts of the Mittelland (the central plateau) and the Alps are dry or very dry. Ticino is the only canton fully out of drought. Reading these as platform regions suggests **at least about 3 regions are "extremely dry" now**; I could not confirm the exact number. [Bote](https://www.bote.ch/nachrichten/schweizundwelt/wetter-schweiz-winter-wird-wohl-nass-und-mild-art-1729932)
- 2026-10-29: The official bulletin says soil-moisture deficits north of the Alps and in the Mittelland are "considerable to extreme". 90-day rainfall deficits are moderate to large almost everywhere, at 50-70% in the Uri and Glarus Alps, Surselva and northern Graubünden. Several river stations show flows that occur only every 10-30 years or less often. Lake Constance, Lake Zurich, Lake Walen and the Jura lakes are well below normal. [Bulletin](https://www.trockenheit.admin.ch/de/trockenheit/trockenheitsbulletin)
- Nothing has settled the question yet.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-04: MeteoSwiss forecasts a dry day nationwide, with fog over the Plateau. [TdG](https://www.tdg.ch/meteo-soleil-en-valais-grisaille-sur-le-plateau-ce-mercredi-197978571446)
- 2026-11-02: Graubünden says water levels in most river basins hit historic lows this summer, and about 5,000 fish were relocated. [swissinfo](https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/emissions-reduction/gr-around-5000-fish-have-been-relocated-due-to-the-drought/92314947)
- 2026-11-02: Klaus Marquardt (Meteo News) expects little rain in the first ten days of November, at most drizzle and fog. He says the strong El Niño may bring a mild, wet winter, but this is uncertain. [Bote](https://www.bote.ch/nachrichten/schweizundwelt/wetter-schweiz-winter-wird-wohl-nass-und-mild-art-1729932)
- 2026-10 (month-end): MeteoSwiss says October was 1.4 °C warmer than normal, with rainfall mostly below average (44-155% of the norm) until shortly before month-end. [bluewin](https://www.bluewin.ch/en/news/the-weather-in-october-was-a-little-too-warm-and-lacked-precipitation-li.3655138)
- 2026-10-16: BAFU says flow deficits are considerable to extreme across much of the country, and several lakes are at extremely low levels for the season. [BAFU](https://www.bafu.admin.ch/de/sommer-2026-trockenheit-und-hohe-wassertemperaturen)
- 2026-10-04: NZZ reports the highest warning level again in large parts of Switzerland. April-September 2026 was the driest summer half-year since records began in 1864, with 56% of normal rainfall. [NZZ](https://www.nzz.ch/wissenschaft/duerre-in-der-schweiz-die-pegel-an-zuerichsee-und-bodensee-sinken-so-tief-wie-noch-nie-ld.10025887) (paywalled; claims taken from search snippets)
- 2026-10-01: SRF says the 2025/26 hydrological year was too dry in all regions, at about 60% of normal rainfall in German-speaking Switzerland. [SRF](https://www.srf.ch/meteo/meteo-stories/ende-des-hydrologischen-jahres-wasser-ist-mangelware)

## 4. Base rates
- The platform has only been running since May 2025, so there is very little history.
- 2026-08-01: 20 of 38 regions were extremely dry. [Blick](https://www.blick.ch/sonntagsblick/wegen-anhaltender-trockenheit-geht-uns-das-trinkwasser-aus-id22151220.html)
- Late August 2026: most of Switzerland was "extremely dry" on the platform. [WSL FAQ](https://www.wsl.ch/de/metanavigation/im-fokus/trockenheit-2026-haeufige-fragen-und-antworten/)
- Early November 2026: about 3 named areas were extremely dry, after late-October rain. The trend since late summer is down, but deficits persist.
- Summer 2025: SRF reported the Rhine Valley at the highest level, described as a 20-30-year event. [SRF](https://www.srf.ch/meteo/meteo-news/trockenheit-in-gewissen-regionen-seit-monaten-zu-wenig-regen)
- Classes can move a lot in a month: from 20 regions in August to a handful in early November. I found no counts for September or October.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the supplied Kalshi or Polymarket markets (Jets, SNB rates, Swiss referendums, Federal Council election, and others) relate to this question. I found no prediction market or expert forecast on the number of drought regions.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-05: next drought bulletin. After that bulletins are roughly weekly, on Thursdays. [Bulletin](https://www.trockenheit.admin.ch/de/trockenheit/trockenheitsbulletin)
- Early November: high pressure keeps conditions dry, and the bulletin says soil-moisture deficits will grow without rain. Later, more frequent westerly rain is expected, roughly normal north of the Alps and below normal in the south. 30- and 90-day deficits are expected to stay as they are, and no lasting groundwater recovery is expected.
- The NOAA monthly model, cited by wetter.com, has November drier than normal, especially in the south and east. This comes from secondary sources and is low reliability. [wetter.com](https://ch.wetter.com/magazin/wetterprognose-und-vorhersage-november_aid_5b55da5238f788063f13ced2.html)
- A strong El Niño might mean a wetter winter; this is uncertain.
- Snow at altitude instead of rain would not ease deficits right away.

**(a) Time left:** About 27 days until resolution on December 1, 2026. About four more weekly platform updates are expected before then.

**(b) Latest known value:** 3 regions classified "Extremely dry" (Lake Zurich region, Glarus Alps, Rhine valley), for the situation up to November 1, 2026. This comes from a news report citing the platform, published November 2, 2026. I could not check it against the platform's own map.

**(c) If nothing changed:** 3 regions.

**(d) If the trend continued:** The count fell sharply from most of the country in August to 3 by November 1, so a continued decline points to about 0 to 2. However, early November is forecast to be dry and the platform describes the situation as continuing. Lake and river levels, which change slowly, may keep these regions extreme, so the decline could stall at around 2 to 4.

**(e) Historical variation:** Month-to-month swings can be large: October brought the count down from widespread extreme drought to 3. In November evaporation is low, so soil-based indices worsen only slowly without rain. Long-window rainfall deficits and low lake and river levels persist even after rain. A plausible range over one month is roughly 0 to about 8, with a tail higher if the dry spell lasts.

**(f) Experts and markets:** No markets exist. MeteoNews expects almost no rain in the first 10 days of November and possibly a wet, mild winter linked to El Niño. A NOAA-based outlook (unverified) suggested a drier-than-normal November in the east and south. The question creator puts the likely range at 2 to 25.

**(g) Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** Strong frontal systems in mid to late November bring heavy rain across the northeast, lifting the Rhine and the lakes. The platform downgrades every region, giving 0.
- **High:** November stays dry with persistent high pressure and fog, the long-window deficits deepen, and the platform's indicators push the Plateau and the eastern regions (Lake Constance, Thurgau, St. Gallen, Zurich) back into extreme. That gives 10 to 18.
